summary: Phase 3 (Wallet + Razorpay mock + Checkout) and Phase 4 (Detailed Order History + Invoice) BACKEND validation. All 19 new tests in /app/backend/tests/test_phase34_wallet_payments_invoice.py PASS. Full backend regression also passes: 50/50 across both test files. Razorpay correctly runs in mock mode (RAZORPAY_KEY_ID empty). Wallet top-up via /api/payments/razorpay/create-order + /api/wallet/razorpay/verify credits the wallet and is idempotent (duplicate=true on replay). Orders work for payment_method in {wallet, razorpay, cod} — razorpay mock flow flips payment_status to 'paid' and persists razorpay_payment_id. Invoice schema correct (invoice_no INV-*, items, subtotal, delivery_fee, wallet_applied, payable, payment_method, payment_status, address, customer) and authZ matrix is correct: owner=200, unauth=401, OTHER customer=403, admin=200. Admin cancel on a fully-wallet-paid order generates a 'refund' wallet_txn and restores balance. ONE NON-BLOCKING BUSINESS-LOGIC GAP: cancelling a partial-wallet order with payment_status='pending' (wallet_applied>0 but payable>0 still owed) does NOT issue a wallet refund because routes/orders.py only refunds when payment_status in ('paid','cod'). Also corrected a stale assertion in the older test_dwaarit_api.py (legacy test asserted total==subtotal, but Phase 3 added a ₹25 flat delivery fee for orders <₹499).

minor.issue: Partial-wallet orders (payment_method='wallet' + payable>0, payment_status remains 'pending') do NOT refund the wallet_applied portion on cancellation. Backend refund gate in routes/orders.py requires payment_status in ('paid','cod'). Consider always refunding wallet_applied regardless of remaining payable, or change payment_status semantics so partially-applied wallet locks count as 'paid' for the wallet portion.

Request body uses the route /api/payments/razorpay/create-order (per /app/backend/routes/payments.py) and NOT /api/payments/order as referenced in the review request. No code change needed — just confirming the actual contract for any future agents.

action_items: (Product decision, non-blocking) Decide whether cancelling a partial-wallet order (payment_status='pending', wallet_applied>0) should refund the wallet_applied portion. If yes, update the refund gate in /app/backend/routes/orders.py to: `if refund_amt > 0 and (order.get('payment_status') in ('paid','cod') or float(order.get('wallet_applied',0)) > 0)` and refund only the wallet_applied portion in that case.
(Doc fix only) Update the review-request template / test_result.md so future iterations call POST /api/payments/razorpay/create-order (not /api/payments/order).
Phase 3/4 backend is GREEN — main agent can proceed with frontend (Phase 3/4) validation.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/payments.py razorpay/verify and wallet/razorpay/verify in mock mode accept ANY signature string. This is correct for mock mode (RAZORPAY_ENABLED=false) but the live code path that calls razorpay_client.utility.verify_payment_signature when RAZORPAY_ENABLED=true should be guarded against missing fields. Verify there's a fail-fast 400 if any of razorpay_order_id/payment_id/signature is missing once real keys are added.

routes/orders.py cancellation path: 'refund_amt = payable + wallet_applied' assumes 'payable' is the post-wallet amount the user actually paid. Confirm payable is consistently stored as the post-wallet payable across all three payment_method branches (wallet/razorpay/cod). For COD orders the user has NOT actually paid yet at cancellation time — issuing a wallet refund of `payable + wallet_applied` for a 'cod' order that's still pending delivery could over-credit the customer. Suggest gating COD refunds on `order.status in ('out_for_delivery','delivered')` or just on COD being already collected.

Wallet topup idempotency is correctly implemented via a unique razorpay_payment_id check — nice. However the create-order endpoint generates a fresh order_mock_<uuid> every call, so the same client can rapidly create N orders. Not a security issue (verify is idempotent on payment_id) but consider rate-limiting /api/payments/razorpay/create-order in production.
